docs(sdk,validation): retire the carriage-committed-evidence framing from the seam comments

Review findings 2-3 on the #620 implementation, plus one site the review
missed (validation-machine.ts): comments and two error messages still
described the auxiliary as hashed into the committed evidence_hash at
prepare and referenced the deleted VerifyReference route. Under the
transition-only commitment (#619) the tier is a build-time delivery
decision the observe-stage door verifies by content, and the reference
wrap happens at ObserveReference. No behavior change; carriage-seam and
proof-fit suites 11/11, typecheck+lint green in both packages.

feat(sdk,fault-proofs,validation): retire the by-hash and carriage staged wires in the TypeScript twins (#620)

The canonical-decode prepare schema collapses to the single four-field
transition-only arm and the item-semantic encoder to the generic
three-field Verify: the by-evidence-hash arm, the carriage redeemer
field, the VerifyReference reference-input route, and the staged
pipeline's proof-item forks are deleted rather than bypassed, and the
staged resolver-0 commitment hashes NoAuxiliaryWitness whatever carriage
the auxiliary names. A chunk-shaped auxiliary now refuses fail-closed at
redeemer construction: the retired four-field wire was the only shape it
could ever have ridden. The shared five-field PrepareSelected schema for
the other eleven phases and the direct-resolve route are untouched.

Tests pin the new wires raw (the committed blueprint moves once, in the
wave's regeneration): the proof-fit fit measurement moves to the observe
stage's inline Observe arm, which now carries the preimage; the
carriage-policy row pins the transition-only source text and the
observe routes; the emulator proof-fit harness deliberately keeps
speaking the deployed wire until the regeneration flips it.

test(validation): pin the transition-only item commitment in the cross-language one-step fixture (#620)

The generator now derives the item-path vector three ways and refuses to
emit on any disagreement: the TypeScript transition-only hash must equal
the base evidence hash (the commitment is over (transition,
NoAuxiliaryWitness)), the retired carriage-committed preimage must
differ from it, and the emitted Aiken test re-checks both equalities on
the other side of the language boundary. The base vectors are
byte-identical to the previous emission, so the producer did not drift.

test(fraud-proofs): prove every transition-only guard can fail across the staged item pipeline (#620)

Thirteen positives walk a genuine field-6 item journey through prepare,
authenticate, and observe under the narrowed commitment; twenty-three
hostile negatives were each run bare (fail markers stripped) against the
full suite to prove the guard they target actually fires: retired-wire
decode refusals for both prepare arms and both semantic arms, swapped
work witnesses and successors, the retired carriage-committed hash, a
substituted certified chunk, flipped carriage bytes on every observe
route, and the deleted observe conjunct's control. Constructor indices
are pinned after the arm retirement with golden wire-layout vectors.

feat(fraud-proofs): narrow the canonical-decode complete-item evidence commitment to the transition alone (#620)

Option B, scoped (spec #619): the prepare stage commits to
hash_one_step_evidence(transition, NoAuxiliaryWitness), computed on-chain;
the by-hash prepare arm and the authenticate stage's carriage argument,
reference-delivery arm, publication-reconstruction helper, and proof-item
parameter are retired; the observe stage keeps both delivery arms and drops
the frozen-hash equality, leaving the section-8.8 field door as the sole
content gate. No shared-library changes. Scratch ABI diff against the fork
baseline moves exactly the three validators (prepare 1788df9b->155131d4,
item-semantic a8d8f3ac->dc88d18e with params 3->2, observe
df695946->146db088); 408 other handler entries unchanged.

docs(evidence): re-pin the accepted CI baseline to the fd941f40 green — empty suite map, Evidence Integrity sole workflow red (#614)

First fully green Midgard Node CI run (32518045121 on fd941f40): all 34
substantive steps passed, including the first-ever executions of the
offline throughput gates and the retained multi-peer DA paths steps.
addendum20260821 records the measurement and re-pins downward under the
E-4 structure: the accepted-red suite map hands forward EMPTY (both
remaining buckets retired as delivered — validationDisputeAccepted by
the wave wirings/rebind, scaffold_issues607_571 by the #607 scanner

Evidence Integrity CI, riding #617's IG1 cascade and re-freeze. No

test(node): key the signature-bridge pre-state by the §5.3 fixed-index item form

Phase B resolves inputs against the Midgard-native spend-input item
encoding (fixed uint16 index, 19 XXXX), not CML's minimal
TransactionInput bytes. The converted-fixture acceptance test predated
that contract and keyed its pre-state with the CML encoding, so the
lookup missed and the accepted-path assertion failed with
E_INPUT_NOT_FOUND. Key it with encodeMidgardSpendInputItemV1 instead.

test(validation,spec,evidence): bind the min-Ada twins on absolute vectors and close D-S4 (#618)

The minimum-Ada floor `coins_per_utxo_byte * (160 + serialized output bytes)`
landed in C49 as two hand-written copies that nothing forced to agree:
`min_ada_lovelace_v1`/`output_meets_min_ada_v1` in
onchain/aiken/lib/midgard/validation-machine-v1.ak and
`minAdaLovelaceV1`/`outputMeetsMinAdaV1` in
demo/midgard-validation/src/value-accounting.ts. Both sides' existing boundary
tests recomputed the expected floor with the formula under test and took the
serialized size from their own encoder, so a slope, intercept, or comparison
change on one side alone kept both suites green.

tests/min-ada-twin-cross-check-v1.test.ts closes that by pinning absolute
lovelace values. Seven vectors carry their floor as a literal, each checked
three ways -- the TypeScript twin, the Aiken twin evaluated from its
checked-in source text through a strict mini-parser that refuses any syntax
the twin is not written in, and the literal itself -- with the
exactly-at-the-floor accept and one-lovelace-below reject legs pinned as
literals too. Two canonical output fixtures are shared with the Aiken side by
absolute CBOR: 41 bytes -> 866_310 and 196 bytes -> 1_534_360 at the C70
snapshot rate, measured byte-identical under `encode_midgard_tx_output` and
`encodeMidgardTxOutput`. Four hostile controls prove the pins are
load-bearing: a moved intercept, a moved slope or added margin, `>=` weakened
to `>`, and a reshaped or absent declaration all fail.

The spec's minimum-UTxO-value rule carried a `\todo` where the ratified
formula belongs (D-S4). It now defines `min_ada_value`, records that the rate
is read from the pinned target-parameter snapshot rather than hard-coded, that
there is no sub-cap and no Midgard margin at any size, that MIN-ADA-TX and
MIN-ADA-UTXO evaluate the same function so both shapes are convictable, and
that the two implementations are held together by the cross-check above.

The C42 manifest row measured green against its pinned 6/6 and 20/20 counts
while its third prescribed evidenceOutput -- the output-scan rejection codes
Q25/Q27/Q35/Q36 bind to -- is absent from the tree: the validation machine
carries 18 distinct reject_* codes, none of them min-Ada, and no E_MIN_ADA
anywhere. The row now says so, names E_MIN_ADA with its five required
consequences, and records that the counts cover the commitment/proof/descriptor
surface only. Q27 records that it covers both violation shapes, and its planned
prescription grows by the two post-block-UTxO selectors, re-pinned from 7 to 9.

The E_MIN_ADA wiring itself, the Aiken-side absolute pins, and the stale
`CML.min_ada_required` comment on the Aiken twin batch into the regeneration
wave (#617).

feat(fault-proofs): refuse an arity mismatch at both compiled-script loading boundaries (#610 ruling)

The #610 ruling (2026-08-18) kept the issue open for the completion its #608
addendum named: the zz605 only-door scan reached only `demo/midgard-sdk/src`
and `demo/midgard-node/src`, so the two fault-proofs loaders stayed outside the
door, and neither of them consulted a validator's declared parameter list.

Both now refuse a mismatch at the load boundary, in the f2629293 shape:

- `src/runtime.ts` `getCompiledScript` deploys `compiledCode` bare for every
  caller, so it refuses any validator that declares parameters, naming the
  count and the declared names. The four titles it loads today
  (`phas.membership.withdraw`, `pexcludes.exclusion.withdraw`,
  `mpf_chunked_verify.verify.withdraw`, `fraud_proof_catalogue.spend.else`)
  declare none, so behaviour is unchanged.
- `tests/support/submit-init-emulator-shared.ts` `getCompiledScript` gets the
  same bare-door refusal, and gains `applyCompiledScript` — an arity-checking
  applying door that refuses too few AND too many terms. The harness's eight
  `applyParamsToScript(getCompiledScript(...), [...])` sites move onto it, so
  it is now the harness's only caller of the unchecked primitive.

Until this landing an arity mismatch surfaced only as an opaque `→ undefined`
evaluation failure a few hundred milliseconds into a submission: applying too
few terms leaves the remaining `validator main(...)` parameters as lambdas, the
ledger's single script-context application reduces to a lambda VALUE, and "no
error" is read as SUCCESS — an always-succeeds script standing where an
authenticated one belongs, which in the emulator is a test that cannot fail.

The scan is extended to `demo/midgard-fault-proofs/src` and
`demo/midgard-fault-proofs/tests` with all six new readers allowlisted and
justified, and each root's yield is now MEASURED and asserted nonzero — a scan
root that collects nothing would leave the set equality passing vacuously.
Measured: 76/2, 228/2, 84/1, 52/5 sources/readers. The bare-door source pin now
covers all three zero-arity doors, and the harness file joins the call-site
count row with `applyCompiledScript` as its helper.

`tests/zz610-compiled-script-arity.test.ts` measures the boundary itself
against the real blueprint. It pins no hash and no parameter count: the
parameterized title used for the positive controls is discovered in the
blueprint at run time. Neutering the three conditions turns exactly its six
refusal rows red and leaves the pass-through rows green.

No .ak or ABI movement; this runs independently of the #617 wave.

Gates (foreground, this tree):
- zz610-compiled-script-arity 12/12; neutered positive control 6 failed / 6 passed
- zz605-semantic-resolver-arity 8/8
- submit-init-emulator-validation-dispute 4/4 in 338s
- typecheck, eslint --max-warnings=0, prettier --check clean

test(fault-proofs): raise the deployment-resolution budget to the 420 s contention precedent (#616)

The V1 validation-dispute resolution row timed out at its 60,000 ms budget
in 2 of the last 4 Midgard Node CI runs and passed in the other 2, on a
step that itself runs ~46 minutes on shared runners. Locally the row
measures ~22 s, so the budget was only ~2.7x the real cost — close enough
that contention alone crosses it. This is a flake, not a slowdown, and it
is in no accepted-red map.

The budget now follows midgard-node's 420 s precedent for
contention-exposed steps rather than the watcher fix's 60 s, which is the
budget that just proved too tight. 420 s also sits inside this suite's
existing per-test range, whose emulator rows already use 120 s to 900 s.

Timeout only — no assertion, fixture, or resolution behaviour changes. Per
#616, a further timeout at this budget is a diagnosis, not another raise.

Suite: 14/14, the affected row at 20,997 ms; typecheck, eslint, prettier
clean.
